name: CureBench
intro: CURE-Bench 是 NeurIPS 2025 治疗推理竞赛基准，评测模型在药物决策、治疗规划、安全性与疗效分析中的多步推理、工具使用和临床可靠性。
build_method: CURE 官网称基于 TxAgent 的 QuestionGen、TraceGen 与 ToolGen；按 TxAgent v1，可证流程是 QuestionGen 生成并验证问题、ToolGen 从 API 文档构建并人工核验 ToolUniverse，二者共同输入 TraceGen 生成和检查答案、工具调用与推理轨迹。CURE 未公开模块提示、筛选规则或移植细节
metric: 官网披露的方案为直接/累积/开放式正确性、改写与选项顺序鲁棒性、Token/工具效率及智能体事实性和临床相关性检查的预定义加权总分；具体权重、裁判配置和最终实现未公开，前 5—10 名专家复核是有效性/取消资格门禁
eval_feature: 赛道一仅用模型内部参数；赛道二可用 ToolUniverse 等生物医学工具并提交工具日志；三种题型的预测、推理、选项与模型/Token/工具元数据打包提交
scale: 官网仅称数千条；精确数量、第一阶段验证/测试规模、第二阶段私有测试规模和不可变数据版本均未公开
build_method_en: CURE says it builds on TxAgent's QuestionGen, TraceGen, and ToolGen. In the pinned TxAgent v1 method, QuestionGen creates and validates questions, ToolGen converts API documentation into human-verified ToolUniverse tools, and validated questions plus ToolUniverse feed TraceGen to generate and check answers, calls, and traces; CURE-specific prompts, filters, and porting details are undisclosed
eval_feature_en: Track 1 uses internal model parameters only; Track 2 may use biomedical tools such as ToolUniverse and must log tool calls. Predictions, reasoning, choices, and model/token/tool metadata cover three question types
intro_en: CURE-Bench is a NeurIPS 2025 therapeutic-reasoning competition benchmark for multi-step drug decision-making, treatment planning, safety and efficacy analysis, tool use, and clinical reliability.
scale_en: The site says thousands; exact count, Phase 1 validation/test sizes, private Phase 2 size, and an immutable public dataset revision are undisclosed
metric_en: The site discloses a planned predefined weighted aggregate of direct/accumulated/open-ended correctness, rephrasing and option-order robustness, token/tool efficiency, and agentic factuality/clinical relevance; exact weights, judge setup, and final implementation are undisclosed, while top-5–10 expert review is a validity/disqualification gate

drawio_review_note: CURE-Bench has no standalone arXiv benchmark paper; its formal primary artifacts are the NeurIPS 2025 competition page and OpenReview proposal rD9YGynuT8. The package is pinned to official site-source commit 5eada4b2c7357ad694a7bf265f546e3e80c067cc, official starter kit 679b08d07d8d1e34197859422b44af5554462b1b, and upstream TxAgent method arXiv:2503.10970v1 (repository 8c24ad9ee2aeb6ca541f63c797d57d7e68502aa4). The CURE site says it is built on TxAgent but does not publish a CURE-specific execution graph; therefore the diagram uses TxAgent v1 only to order the reusable modules: QuestionGen verifies grounding, solvability, and reasonableness; ToolGen creates ToolUniverse through API summarization, specification generation, checker tests, and human verification; validated questions and ToolUniverse then feed TraceGen, which evaluates answers, function calls, and reasoning traces. TxAgent's 211 tools, 85,340 questions/traces, and other training counts are not CURE counts. The site names 12 named task families, while its correctness section says 13 tasks; these counts are unreconciled. The starter kit documents Phase 1 validation/test data and a private Phase 2 final test, but there is no public dataset revision or official split size. The site says thousands only. Track 1 forbids external tools; Track 2 allows ToolUniverse and requires a tool log. The site discloses a predefined weighted evaluation plan, while the pinned starter-kit README says final metrics would be announced with final results; exact weights, prompts, judge configuration, and realized implementation remain unpublished. Top-5–10 human expert review is a metric-hacking validity/disqualification gate, not a numeric score term.
